# Necessity Knows no Law. 

Dawn warms some strange and subtile world,   
New growth creeps from cracked bleached bones.  
The world grows welcome, as death's visage grins on

It’s been three years since the events of Operation Cold Storage, The ramifications of the “Ringing heard round the world” have rattled the whole world, and yet life always goes on. One would think that nothing would surprise you anymore, but the matrix has gotten “weird” AF and that’s got everyone on edge. Everyone with even a shred of authority has gotten so tight-lipped, the silence is starting to speak volumes. A new BTL is making the rounds, except this time it’s different, you can take your favorite BTL personality and bring them into the real world\! Be Johnny Cash walking down the street, Sing as if you’re  fuchsia dragons roaring down the street\!   
The Matrix is what your grandaddy called what is now everywhere. The grey goo ate the world, and spit it back up whole as indigestion. It’s had some weird after effects, everything has a matrix signature now so Mr. Old timer, no body mods, no electronics doohickies, is still lit up like a christmas tree because the water he drinks, the air he breathes, the shit synth meat burrito he ate for lunch are all crawling with nanites. Welcome to the 6th world, kicking and screaming\! This means, all the hacker types are all bullshitting you if they tell you they can hack shit anymore. The Technomancers, are so deep in their own shit that they can be on par with the Matrix critters out there, but your everyday code slinger? That drek is now sim staple drama \- made for TV (who’s even seen one of those before?) shit. Now we have Sprites, and it’s not your everyday Sprites, these bad mo-fo’s they have teeth and personality. Rumor says they can manifest, (well sorta, it’s like when a pile of nanites all swarm into a nanite ball and munch a toaster and then the toaster can wiggle around a bit. It’s funny until the next time you wanna make toast\!) So what’s a poor cyber weenie to do? Well, what they’ve always done, shitpost and make alliances. If Sprites are so hot shit, then recruit their asses and put them to work\! (Each sprite has a power level that is generally tied to their intelligence and personality, smarter \== harder to control/work with, and if they’re too smart maybe you’ll end up working for them…)   
The other ramification is that AI now are dual natured, it’s weird, like really weird. It’s not common but some of the most badass sorcery ever slung has been between AI and Dragons… like rocking the world level shit. There’s some  video of it that got snuck onto the matrix a while back and wooo boy, fireworks and shenanigans. Looks like something out of a horror movie honestly. Half the pundits can’t decide if it’s real, and the others are screaming about the end of times. It must be that time of year again, because we’re on like our seventh, end of times and these prologs keep on rolling…  
	So what’s new is old. Capitalism keeps on working the angles, unfathomable horrors compete with each other for their time on the news, there’s no substitute for hard work, and damnet, where is my flying car\!  
	

# Beasterary: 

## Obsidiman

![][image1]  
In glacial geothermal areas all around the world, strange rock and crystal creatures have emerged. Some of them have taken the shapes of various meta humans, while others look chiseled from  fresh rock face.  

 

1. [Obsidiman](https://shadowrun.fandom.com/wiki/Obsidiman) \- Obsidimen are a race of large, rock-based humanoids. They stand over 7 feet tall and weigh over 900 pounds. Their primary connection is to their Liferock, which is a large formation of stone within four hours of their place of birth. Obsidimen are loyal to the community around their Liferock, and eventually return to it. Obsidimen can live around 500 years away from their Liferock, and their ultimate lifespan is unknown, as they generally return to it and remain there. Due to their rocky nature and long lives, obsidimen are rather slow moving and deliberate in both speech and action, and can have difficulty understanding the smaller races' need for haste. However, if aroused by a threat to self, friend, or community, obsidimen are fearsome to behold.

## Ghosts 

**"In any form, ghosts look like a stiff breeze might disrupt them. They appear faint, like tenth-generation copies of a spirit, but they pay no heed to summoners trying to conjure them. Could they be astral representations of the dead? Maybe. Maybe not. No matter how long I’ve looked, I’ve yet to find my grandfather in astral space." Street Grimoire pg. 190 under "Ghosts"**  
Ghost exist in the SR rpg universe and they range from the disturbing like the Shattergraves which has a huge number of them, to the dangerous like the ‘lemurs’ of Madagascar where the ghosts of the 10 million who died there are trapped on the island and want out.

Ghosts are effectively minor forms of spirits and there are subject to summoning and binding. They tend to be far less powerful or useful than spirits unless you are seeking a specific piece of information from a dead person’s ghost.

A ghost that has had time to build up some power can have a domain where they are a real threat, typically their home in life or the place where they died. In these places they can often express spirit powers.

There are also e-ghosts which may or may not be actual spirits of people who died while online. There were a lot of people connected during the Crash 2.0 and months after their deaths some people reported seeing their avatars or getting messages from the dead people. When I last played SR these e-ghosts were new and it wasn’t certain if they were technomantic spirits of the machine or simply fragments of code that thought they were people.

### Sister Sinalma

Brilliant former wizard and cyber surgeon at a delta grade clinic run by Aztechnology in Peru.  Got interested in HMHVV and the potential to offset essence loss from augmentation.  Used herself as a test subject, and knew everything she needed to hide her raging augmentation addiction and rapidly deepening cyberpsychosis from the rest of the research team.  Wound up wiping out half the compound when she cracked during a routine performance test.  Escaped from the smoking crater of the facility, converted to Catholicism, and is now  putting her head back together and seeking redemption as a member of a convent devoted to Santa Rosa de Lima, which happens to have interests which overlap the plot in some fashion.  Use like Hannibal Lechter from Silence of the Lambs \- friendly deeply disturbed predator that should leave the characters feeling like they're getting swimming instructions from a great white shark.

###  Cleo:

It’s Cleo, and I know what you’re thinking. Cliche'  right? "red pill" or the "blue pill", a choice between seeing the world between worlds, or staying fat, dumb and happy as you are. What’s in it? Red Pill’s a chance to come back alive, no matter what, and the blue pill keeps you as your mamma, or whatever flea dirt ripper doc made you. 

It’s Cleo, and I know what you’re thinking. Cliche'  right? "red pill" or the "blue pill", a choice between seeing the world between worlds, or staying fat, dumb and happy as you are. What’s in it? Red Pill’s a chance to come back alive, no matter what, and the blue pill keeps you as your mamma, or whatever flea dirt ripper doc made you. Here are the rewinder reasons. 1\) It's a ride. Sure the scenery changes with the weather, but the ride is always the same: you get up and go to work. In red pill you accept that life is going to be tedious if you're lazy. What’s not to like about that? 2\) It shows how the world really is. The blue pill is a lie. Real life is brutal, no matter what, except for the leechers that lead you around by the nose. Or those who claim that real life is filled with opulence and wealth and all the things people desire. That's a lie too, a sellout to the fat, dumb and happy world. Red pill says "shit. The world is just like you’d expect and it’s shit. A lot of fat, dumb and happy people know it, too. But there are many, many, many others, and they don't give a fuck." The blue pill says "life is a struggle and being successful is hard." It doesn't stop there, it goes on to say "if you're not good at something, get better at it. If it’s easy to get, make yourself tough enough to not get it. If you have to work hard, well, it means you are a winner." No surprise there. Red pill tells you "your life is shit. You're a loser. It's gonna be shitty for the next however many years." The blue pill has you assuming that as a lazy poofter you're gonna turn things around, and there’s a big fat zero chance that you’re gonna do that. We all make choices, and red pill makes you confront the shit. 3\) The blue pill betrays who you are. Imagine if a relationship where you had a major personality clash suddenly got better. Blue pill says "well, this person's not a total poofter, but they’re not the greatest either. I guess we're decent. Won't we be able to work together in the future?" Red Pill says "this person betrayed me. If I want to have any chance of a good relationship I have to cut this person out of my life." Blue pill says "well, they're not bad people, but we have to work on the relationship anyway." Not when red pill tells you that the relationship is bad. 4\) It’s a matter of survival. You know what’s easier than telling a kid “well, kids are no good, but if you work hard at it you can get good at this.” It’s having to actually face this, and figure it out. It’s far more terrifying. 5\) Red pill is life-changing. When you face your mortality and the fact that you’re just a sperm in the wind, you tend to look at things with a new outlook. It’s not about stuff like "getting a new car” or “buying that new car”, and watching the world pass you by. It’s about dealing with the moment, and accepting the consequences of it. There’s a lesson to be learned in it, and the truth of it is scarier than any blue pill could ever be. You may think that blue pill is better, but it’s just as much a lie. This red pill shit is real, and it will change your life. Red pill is life-changing.

So what’s the deal with this red pill bullshit? I got an email from a German chap, who calls himself Francky, saying “I have read your post on what it means to be a red-pill man. I also got into philosophy when I was in high school and was looking for an answer to what the meaning of life is. When I got into philosophical questions, I came across the red pill and thought to myself, what does this mean?”

Francky goes on to tell me about his family and how he struggles with them, but says that the red pill really does make him confront things:

“When I’m around my family, it feels like I’m working in a job for them, to keep the family together. Whenever I get upset about that, I read the red-piller’s posts and try to give an explanation, which is something that does help me.”

Francky said that he has a few friends who have been taken on to red pill stuff, and he has started reading the same thing they are reading. He said he wants to show them his understanding of things, and get them to see that he sees things differently.

I asked Francky what his biggest problem is and I think he summed it up pretty well:

“The problem is that I want the red pill to be something that’s related to philosophy. I want it to be clear, but if it’s so black and white, I feel like I don’t understand anything. Sometimes, my family members don’t take anything I say serious, so I try to talk about it with someone. But since most of them only get what the red-piller tells them, I feel like they don’t see that I have thoughts on things, and I feel like they’re too sure of themselves.”

I think Francky has it wrong. I think that it’s exactly because of the black and white approach that red pill does make sense. After all, if you’re relying on blue pill philosophy to guide you, you’re not going to get anywhere. As Francky pointed out to me, if you have a problem, the blue pill will tell you the opposite of what

### Darri

Darri theorized that meteorite could sense their thoughts. And it knew what they were missing. Thereby, it created people based on the thoughts and feelings of those close to it (residents of Zkazena). But these changelings were not the absolute personality of the lost ones. They were instead a manifestation of their thoughts and everything they were going through. For example, Darri’s son Mikael showed signs of psychopathy because it was all Darri remembered about Mikael. Darri blamed his son for his divorce, which for Darri was a phenomenon similar to death. 

A similar layer could be perceived in Grima’s case, who resurrected her sister Asa through her thoughts. Grima never recovered from the disappearance of Asa and kept on playing with the memories. Because the thoughts were affectionate, the changeling image of Asa acted moderately. Yet, she lacked a purpose in life because her creator Grima had none in mind.

# Philosophy and Themes:

## Personafix

What if a BTL didn’t work just in the matrix, but you could take that experience into the real world, walk around and have a movie star in your head, saying cool things and doing awesome things while you get to experience it all  
These new Waking Dreams, are the new big craze, although theres a dark side, celebrities are denying they ever made them and celebrity families are complaining about strangers calling and claiming to be their dad or mom. Law enforcement had to be called in. 

 

* [Setting](https://shadowrun-portland.obsidianportal.com/search?tag=Setting)

A variant form of BTL is the “personafix chip,” which transforms the personality, thoughts, and memories of the user to a particular personality, usually famous. A person slotting a personafix chip of Maria Mercurial, for example, believes that he or she is Maria Mercurial, and reacts with the emotions and personality of the starlet.

These chips are popularly used in [Bunraku (or Meat puppet) Parlors](https://shadowrun-portland.obsidianportal.com/wikis/bunraku-parlor), where the prostitute can become any personality the buyer desires. Modified personafix chips are also used in covert infiltration, to enhance the acting and disguise of a mole.

## Leónization

Leónization (named for Ponce de León, a Renaissance explorer who sought the Fountain of Youth) is a [genetic](https://shadowrun.fandom.com/wiki/Genetic_Engineering) anti-aging treatment that rejuvenates the body at the cellular level.  
A potent combination of [nanite](https://shadowrun.fandom.com/wiki/Nanotechnology) gene therapy and cellular repair, it restores the individual to the approximate physique and youth of a young adult. It is not known if there are any negative side effects from long term use and repeated treatments. The technique also is prohibitively expensive, with a cost in the millions of [nuyen](https://shadowrun.fandom.com/wiki/Nuyen), and thus remains only within the grasp of the rich and powerful.  
To participate, the individual must stay within a nutrient bath for at least four months, with semi-annual "touch-up" sessions for the next few years. It is rumored that after a certain number of treatments, the subject's cells start to spontaneously degenerate and break down, causing death within hours.

## What lies in the ballance

Moral question: Can any reparation for act from the past, make up for wrongs committed today. If jews deserve palestine, do native Americans deserve america? Do Catalan deserve independence from Spain? Will Ireland ever heal and forgive Britain? How long must a grudge endure? Until the last woman, man and child have it wiped from their collective memories?

[https://essays.georgestrakhov.com/elvish/](https://essays.georgestrakhov.com/elvish/)This was written in the context of describing human technology progression, but it would also make a handy way to think about presenting elves in a RPG setting.

## Horri or horrors, it’s just a name, but what is it?

Like what makes Horrors so scary this time around is that they appear that they can be reasoned with, and so we project human motives onto them when their motives are so alien and their logic so foreign that we fool ourselves into believing our own mirror.

It wasn't destroying. It was changing everything. It was making something new.

## Death is just the beginning

Growth, it incorporates pieces around it and remake them into something new. Something tired and old can have new life breathed back into it, but what if that growth was seen as “un-natural” Death is death, and gone is gone, but what if you could pick up the pieces after they’ve fallen down and pick them back up, fill in the gaps and make it beautiful in the eye of the beholder?

## Death becomes you.

You can't die, well you sort of can and we'll it's messy and you only get a few options on what you can do with the rest of your extra life.   
You're Not You Anymore. You're a snipped thread tied into a new string, you look wrong, smell wrong, act wrong and feel wrong but the more you feel the contour of the knot keeping you together, the more terrified you become of it slipping undone. It drives you like nothing before. Whatever your driving motivation is, it's amped to 11\.   
Nothing is free and getting tied down has its own strings attached. You now OWE something to someone big time. Maybe that life contract with that free spirit wasn't such a good idea, or was it the one up token that lit you up when you picked it up. In some cases, you're tied to a particular object, or a particular place. You may have a new familiar with you or see creatures and beings that you don't recognize from the corner of your eye.   
Being brought back is like being taken apart piece by piece by a being that loves and understands you like nothing before. It cuts through your self loathing and cynicism, and gives you a glimpse of what bliss feels like. It's a religious experience, but there is no god unless you pretend really hard and don't think about the reality of the situation. Coming back together, something always feels off, like a sharp pain that isn't there or a grinding of your bones that feels off. 

 Imagine dying frightened and in pain and having that as the only part of you which survives.

## Ole Miners Pharmacy (closed \- or is it?)

One of the last businesses out of Zkazena,  a modern day ghost town.  
   
The Zkazena area became the most productive lead-zinc mining field in the district producing over $20 billion worth of ore between 1917 and 1947\. More than fifty percent of the lead and zinc metal used during World War I were produced by the Zkazena district. At its peak over 14,000 miners worked the mines and another 4,000 worked in mining services. Many of these workers commuted by an extensive trolley system from as far away as Joplin and Carthage, Missouri. Mining ceased in 1967 and water pumping from the mines ceased. The contaminated water from some 14,000 abandoned mine shafts, 70 million tons of mine tailings, and 36 million tons of mill sand and sludge remained as a huge environmental cleanup problem.The area became part of the Tar Creek Superfund site.  
   
On April 24, 2006, Reuters reported that Zkazena had been scheduled to be closed and all residents removed. Due in large part to the removal of large amounts of subsurface material during mining operations, many of the city's structures have been deemed in imminent danger of caving in  
   
The city's pharmacist, Gary Linderman was featured in the May 28, 2007, issue of People magazine in the Heroes Among Us article "Prescription for Kindness". He vowed to stay as long as there was anyone left who needed him and to be the last one out of the city.

# **Necessity Knows No Law: An Analysis of Survival, Power, and Extralegal Imperatives in a Fractured World**

## **Introduction: Defining Necessity in a Broken World**

# The maxim "Necessity knows no law" typically suggests moments of extreme duress where legal or ethical constraints are bypassed for survival. However, in the context of a world grappling with profound environmental devastation, unchecked corporate power, resurgent and alien supernatural forces, transformative technologies, and echoes of ancient existences, this phrase transcends proverbial status. It becomes a fundamental operating principle, a constant pressure shaping societies, driving conflicts, and defining the motivations of individuals, organizations, and even non-human entities. This world operates under the shadow of various necessities – the need to survive a poisoned environment, the corporate imperative for profit and control, the existential requirement to defend against inhuman horrors, the drive to adapt to or exploit radical biological and digital transformations, and the pull of ancient, non-metahuman imperatives. These forces routinely compel actions that exist outside, against, or simply orthogonal to the established legal and ethical frameworks designed for a simpler, more stable reality. The inherent conflict is not merely between legality and illegality, but between the fragile constructs of imposed order – laws, regulations, corporate policies, social norms – and the fundamental, often brutal, drivers of existence itself.

# The pressures forcing entities beyond the bounds of law are diverse and interconnected. Environmental collapse, exemplified by ecological sacrifice zones like the Tar Creek Superfund site 1, creates desperate necessities for basic survival, forcing inhabitants into risky and illicit activities simply to endure. The rise of megacorporations, such as Wuxing Incorporated 3, establishes parallel systems of power where the 'laws' of profit and market dominance supersede public statutes, compelling employees and competitors alike into shadow economies and extralegal competition. Supernatural threats, ranging from the insidious infiltration of Insect Spirits 5 to the potentially world-ending incursions of Horrors 7, demand responses so extreme – preemptive violence, forbidden magic, societal upheaval – that conventional legality becomes a secondary, often irrelevant, concern. Concurrently, technological advancements rewrite the very definition of life and necessity. Treatments like Leonization offer near-immortality to the elite, creating necessities tied to status and power maintenance that operate outside normal lifecycles.9 The HMHVV virus spawns new metahuman variants like ghouls, whose biological necessities clash with societal norms and laws.11 The emergence of Technomancers 13, Artificial Intelligences, and the exploitative technology of Bunraku parlors 15 introduces new forms of consciousness, existence, and subjugation that defy easy legal categorization and control. Finally, the potential re-emergence of ancient beings like Obsidimen 17 brings primordial necessities, tied to geological cycles and non-metahuman biology, into conflict with the structures of the modern world.

# In such a complex and pressured environment, "Necessity Knows no Law" is not an exception but the pervasive rule. It dictates the flow of power, the struggle for resources, the nature of conflict, and the moral landscape inhabited by all beings. This analysis will explore how these various pressures, drawn from documented events and entities, weave together to create a world where the dictates of necessity consistently override the constraints of law, shaping a reality defined by extralegal imperatives and the constant struggle for existence.

## **Section 1: The Poisoned Earth \- Survival in Sacrifice Zones**

# The legacy of industrial progress often leaves behind scarred landscapes where the environment itself becomes an antagonist, forcing inhabitants into a state of perpetual, lawless necessity. The Tar Creek Superfund site in northeastern Oklahoma serves as a stark blueprint for such "sacrifice zones".1 Originally exploited for its rich deposits of lead and zinc, crucial for munitions production during both World Wars 1, the region's initial contribution to national necessity laid the groundwork for a protracted environmental and human catastrophe. Decades of mining and milling operations, ceasing primarily in the 1960s and 70s, left behind staggering volumes of toxic waste – over 500 million tons in the Tri-State area.1 This waste, locally termed "chat," consists of crushed rock tailings containing hazardous concentrations of lead, zinc, and cadmium.1 These contaminants litter the surface in massive piles, some towering nearly 200 feet, covering thousands of acres, often immediately adjacent to homes and schools.2

# The consequences of this legacy are devastating and pervasive. Heavy metals from the chat piles and abandoned mine workings leach into the soil and water systems.1 Approximately 300 miles of unsealed underground mine tunnels and thousands of boreholes became conduits for contamination.1 When pumping operations ceased with the mines' abandonment, groundwater refilled these voids, reacting with oxidized minerals to create highly acidic mine water.1 By 1979, this toxic brew began discharging into surface waters like Tar Creek, turning the water a distinctive, corrosive orange due to iron oxides and decimating aquatic life.21 The contamination severely impacted vital aquifers, including the Boone and Roubidoux, sources of drinking water 1, with lead and cadmium levels measured at five times national standards in the early 1980s.21 The land itself became unstable, prone to subsidence as mine roofs collapsed or shafts eroded.1 Most critically, the contamination directly harmed the human population. Children, the most vulnerable group, exhibited alarmingly high rates of elevated blood lead levels – studies in the 1990s showed rates of 35% among Native American children and 43% among young children in the mining area generally, far exceeding CDC thresholds and state averages.1 These exposures are linked to learning disabilities, neurological damage, and other severe health problems.21

# Despite designation as a Superfund site in 1983 1, official responses proved tragically inadequate for the scale of the disaster. Various cleanup attempts targeting surface water occurred through the 80s and 90s.1 Later efforts focused on remediating residential yards and high-access areas, removing millions of tons of source material.1 However, the site spans 40 square miles 19, making comprehensive remediation incredibly costly and complex.2 Recognizing the intractable nature of the problem, the government instituted voluntary buyout programs, transferring ownership of properties in the most hazardous zones (like Picher and Cardin) to entities like the Local Industrial Community Recovery Action Trust (LICRAT) and ultimately to the Quapaw Nation, the original stewards of the land who had leased it to mining companies under exploitative historical terms.1 Yet, even with these efforts, significant contamination and populations remain.2

# Within this poisoned landscape, the necessity of survival dictates actions that disregard legal boundaries. Resource scarcity becomes acute. With soil and water poisoned, obtaining safe food and drink may require accessing restricted areas, participating in black markets, or stealing resources. The ubiquitous chat waste, despite its known toxicity, was historically used as fill material and road gravel, even in yards and playgrounds 2 – a practice born perhaps of ignorance initially, but potentially continued out of sheer necessity for basic construction materials in an impoverished area. Health and safety become paramount drivers of extralegal behavior. Residents unable or unwilling to accept buyouts might resort to illicit means to secure medical treatment for lead poisoning or other exposure-related illnesses, or find ways to illegally occupy safer, abandoned properties. The failure of the state and responsible parties to provide a safe environment or adequate remediation creates a vacuum where individual or community necessity must find its own solutions, regardless of legality. Furthermore, the deep sense of injustice stemming from decades of environmental degradation and health impacts, often disproportionately affecting marginalized communities like the resident Native American tribes 2, can fuel extralegal forms of protest, resistance, or even vigilantism against perceived corporate or governmental negligence.19 The community tragedy fosters a spirit where fighting back becomes a necessity, potentially outside established legal channels.

# These sacrifice zones, therefore, evolve beyond mere wastelands. The persistent failure of legal and official systems to address the fundamental necessities of life – clean water, safe housing, health – transforms these areas into incubators for alternative, often illicit, social and economic structures. Black markets thrive, informal networks replace official services, and unique cultural adaptations to extreme environmental stress emerge. The constant pressure of survival fosters social dynamics centered on resilience and mutual aid, but also potentially on ruthless competition for scarce resources, all operating largely outside the purview of formal law. This extreme environmental stress, coupled with the desperation of the inhabitants, might also create unique conditions for novel biological adaptations or even attract specific kinds of supernatural phenomena drawn to the suffering and decay, linking the environmental necessity to the magical and biological transformations explored later.

# Moreover, the history of Tar Creek exemplifies a destructive cycle. The initial "necessity" – the extraction of lead and zinc for wartime munitions, sanctioned and encouraged by the state 1 – directly created the toxic legacy. This state-approved imperative, driven by national security and economic goals, ignored long-term consequences, ultimately generating a new, more desperate form of necessity for the communities left behind: the necessity of daily survival in a poisoned world, often requiring actions deemed illegal by the very system that created the hazard. This pattern suggests a recurring theme where short-term, officially sanctioned necessities sow the seeds for long-term, lawless struggles driven by the fundamental need to endure the consequences.

## **Section 2: The Gilded Cage \- Megacorporate Order and the Laws of Profit**

# While environmental collapse forces extralegal action from the bottom up through sheer survival needs, the dominance of megacorporations imposes its own form of necessity from the top down, operating under a distinct set of 'laws' dictated by profit, power, and influence. Wuxing Incorporated, a major player on the global stage, serves as an illustrative case study of how corporate imperatives can reshape the legal landscape and compel others into the shadows.3 Originating as an import/export business in Hong Kong, potentially engaging in smuggling against Communist Chinese restrictions 4, Wuxing demonstrated ambition and opportunism from its inception. Its founder, Wu Kuan-Lei, actively supported the Hong Kong Free Enterprise Zone, supplying arms and expertise.4 Under his son, Wu Lung-Wei, the corporation weathered the Crash of '29, strategically acquiring failed allies to expand its reach.4 A pivotal moment came with the reading of the great dragon Dunkelzahn's will, which bequeathed Wuxing significant capital (200 million nuyen funneled into magical R\&D), a powerful magical focus (the Jade Dragon of Wind and Fire), and the Third Coin of Luck to CEO Wu Lung-Wei's wife, Sharon Chiang-Wu.3 These boons catalyzed Wuxing's rapid ascent from a regional AA-rated corporation 23 to a AAA-rated global megacorporation and member of the prestigious Corporate Court.3 This growth was further solidified through strategic alliances, notably the formation of the Pacific Prosperity Group (PPG) alongside corporations like Yamatetsu, expressly aimed at countering Japancorp influence in the Pacific Rim.3

# Wuxing's power stems from a diversified portfolio encompassing finance, shipping, consumer goods, chemicals, agriculture, engineering, and, significantly, magical goods and services.3 Subsidiaries like Wuxing Financial Services, Prosperity Development Corporation, Wuxing Worldwide Shipping, Red Wheel Engineering, and Eastern Electronics solidify its presence across multiple sectors.3 Its corporate culture, while outwardly described as quiet and conservative 22, is deeply steeped in Chinese traditions 22, particularly the Wuxing magical tradition practiced by its *wujen*.25 This tradition centers on the concept of *qi* (life force), the five elements (fire, water, earth, wood, metal), and the balance of yin and yang.25 Wuxing leverages this unique asset, focusing on magical research, particularly involving Spirits of the Elements 3, and employing geomancy – the manipulation of *qi*, *feng shui*, and mana flows along ley lines or "dragon lines" – as a core competency.25 *Wujen* utilize ritual magic to adjust background mana counts and align energy flows, often collaborating on *feng shui* projects to optimize corporate facilities for prosperity and potentially disrupt rivals' energetic harmony.25

# The actions driven by Wuxing's corporate necessities – profit maximization, market expansion, competitive advantage, internal security – frequently operate outside or directly counter to conventional public law, creating environments where others are compelled into illegality. A key factor is megacorporate extraterritoriality.24 AAA-rated corporations often possess sovereign territory where their own internal rules and security forces hold sway, effectively placing them above the laws of the nations they operate within. Wuxing's necessity to secure resources, eliminate competition, or cover up damaging incidents might lead to actions within its enclaves that would be criminal elsewhere, carried out with impunity. Its significant financial power 3 allows for market manipulation, predatory lending, or hostile takeovers that can create severe economic necessity for individuals, smaller businesses, or even governments, pushing them towards debt, desperation, and potentially shadow work or criminal enterprise simply to survive the economic fallout.

# Wuxing's mastery of geomancy introduces a more subtle, yet potentially profound, method of extralegal influence. The ability to manipulate *feng shui* and mana flows isn't merely about optimizing office layouts or enhancing magical research 25; it represents a potential tool for large-scale environmental and economic engineering. By adjusting ley lines or disrupting the *qi* of a rival's territory 29, Wuxing could theoretically create localized zones of prosperity or hardship, influencing migration patterns, property values, agricultural yields, or even ambient magical potential.25 Such actions, driven by the necessity of gaining a competitive edge or securing resources, operate far outside the scope of conventional environmental regulations or economic laws, functioning as a form of covert geopolitical manipulation. This expertise might also lead Wuxing to view environmentally devastated areas like Tar Creek not as liabilities, but as opportunities.30 Such zones might possess unique or disrupted geomantic properties ripe for study or exploitation, or offer environments with minimal oversight where dangerous research or resource extraction can occur, driven by corporate necessity that overrides ethical or environmental concerns.

# Ultimately, megacorporations like Wuxing don't just exist within the legal system; they create parallel systems governed by their own internal necessities. Profit, growth, security, and internal politics become the de facto laws within their sphere of influence.24 Employees, contractors, and even shadowrunners hired by or targeting the corporation must navigate this internal landscape.24 Fulfilling corporate objectives, gaining promotions, or simply surviving within the corporate structure often requires actions that bend or break external laws – industrial espionage, sabotage, data theft, suppression of inconvenient truths. The corporation's definition of necessity thus fosters and sustains a "shadow" ecosystem, an entire sphere of extralegal activity that becomes necessary for functioning within or interacting with the corporate world. The quiet, conservative facade 22 may mask a reality where necessity dictates ruthless, lawless action as standard operating procedure.

## **Section 3: Beyond the Veil \- Supernatural Imperatives and Metahuman Responses**

# The return of magic has not only reawakened latent metahuman potential but also opened pathways for entities whose existence and imperatives operate entirely outside metahuman comprehension and law. Confronting these supernatural threats forces individuals and organizations into extreme measures, driven by necessities that dwarf conventional legal and ethical considerations.

### **Subsection 3.1: The Hive and the Host \- Insect Spirits**

# Among the most insidious threats are the Insect Spirits, or *invae*.31 These are not merely awakened terrestrial insects but alien, transdimensional invaders hailing from crowded, hostile metaplanes.5 Incapable of manifesting directly on the physical plane like typical spirits, they require living metahuman hosts.5 Through a ritual process called investment or merging, often involving unwilling victims captured and cocooned 31, the insect spirit fuses with the host's body.5 This process invariably destroys the host's original spirit or consciousness 6, fundamentally altering the host's physical form to varying degrees. Some merges result in grotesque, insectoid monstrosities 6, while others, particularly those involving strong-willed hosts or specific spirit types like female Mantids, result in "Good Merges".5 These hosts retain their original appearance, memories, and skills, allowing the inhabiting spirit to act as a perfect infiltrator, undetectable by mundane means and even capable of masking its magical aura.31

# The fundamental drive of most Insect Spirits is propagation: to establish hives, convert more hosts, and potentially terraform the environment to better suit their existence.5 They exhibit cunning intelligence, sophisticated deception, and often operate with hive-mind coordination.5 Their social structures mirror terrestrial insects, with specialized roles like Workers, Soldiers, Caretakers, Scouts, and Nymphs.34 Different species exhibit distinct behaviors, from the highly organized and territorial Ants to the migratory, consuming swarms of Locusts.34 The infamous Universal Brotherhood, a seemingly benevolent organization advocating for metahuman rights, was revealed to be a front for Insect Spirits, harvesting the vulnerable and dispossessed to expand their numbers.5 At the heart of a developed hive often lies a Queen or Mother spirit, immensely powerful entities capable of summoning more spirits independently, representing the greatest threat.6

# The existential and insidious nature of the Insect Spirit threat – body-snatching, infiltration, potential planetary conversion – necessitates responses that frequently operate outside the law. Standard law enforcement and legal procedures are utterly inadequate to address hosts who may appear perfectly normal or hives hidden within mundane structures. The necessity of preventing infestation and eliminating hives before they grow uncontrollable (as seen in the case of Chicago, which required extreme measures including a tactical nuclear device – the Cermak Blast – to contain 5) justifies actions that violate fundamental rights and legal norms. Suspected hosts may face summary execution without due process. Entire buildings or city blocks might be destroyed to eradicate a hive, regardless of property rights or collateral damage. Organizations or individuals fighting the threat might resort to forbidden magic, dangerous alliances (such as collaborating with predatory Mantis spirits, who hunt other *invae* but are not allies of metahumanity 5), or impose draconian quarantines that disregard individual liberties.

# The existence of "Good Merges" creates a particularly potent necessity for paranoia and extralegal measures. When the enemy can look identical to a friend, neighbor, or colleague 5, trust evaporates. The need to identify these hidden threats before they can facilitate a wider infestation fosters an environment where invasive magical or technological surveillance, profiling based on suspicion rather than evidence, preemptive detention, or even elimination become thinkable, perhaps even necessary, actions. Legal protections like privacy and presumption of innocence become luxuries unaffordable in the face of such a hidden, existential threat.

# Furthermore, a deeply disturbing possibility arises from the connection between Insect Spirits and the even greater threat of the Horrors. Some lore suggests that Insect Spirit hives, while horrific in themselves, might serve as a buffer against the Horrors, instinctively attacking them when they encroach.33 This introduces a potential "lesser evil" dilemma of terrifying proportions. Could it become necessary to tolerate, or even cultivate, an Insect Spirit infestation in a specific area to delay or defend against the arrival of the Horrors? Such a decision, weighing one existential threat against another, operates entirely outside any conceivable legal or conventional ethical framework, driven solely by the grim calculus of ultimate survival.

### **Subsection 3.2: Facing the Scourge \- Horrors**

# If Insect Spirits represent an insidious existential threat, the Horrors embody apocalypse.7 These are not merely powerful spirits but malevolent, often god-like entities hailing from the deepest, most alien metaplanes.35 They can only cross into our reality when ambient magic levels reach cyclical peaks.7 Their nature is diverse and terrifying, ranging from bestial eating machines to hyper-intelligent, manipulative beings that feed on the fear, pain, and suffering they inflict.7 Their presence warps reality itself, creating toxic magical environments 6, and their arrival *en masse* constitutes an event known as the Scourge – a period of devastation that, in previous magic cycles like the Fourth World (Earthdawn), forced civilizations to hide in magically sealed underground shelters (kaers) for centuries.8

# The motivations of Horrors seem primarily predatory and malicious; they exist to cause harm and feed on the resulting negative emotions.7 While some, like the "Named Horrors" (e.g., Nemesis, Bonecrown 35), exhibit complex strategies involving political manipulation or economic exploitation, the fundamental consensus among those knowledgeable (like Immortal Elves and Great Dragons) is that Horrors cannot be reasoned or bargained with.8 They represent a fundamental cosmic antagonism to life as metahumanity understands it.

# Confronting the Horrors, or even the *threat* of their premature arrival due to mana spikes or deliberate manipulation 8, represents the ultimate necessity, justifying any action, no matter how extreme or unlawful. The scale of the threat renders metahuman legal systems utterly insignificant. Countermeasures operate on a cosmic scale and involve powers and sacrifices beyond conventional understanding. Great Dragons like Dunkelzahn may sacrifice themselves to erect metaphysical barriers or level out mana fluctuations to delay their arrival.8 Immortal Elves like Harlequin engage in millennia-long machinations against them.8 Forbidden practices like blood magic might be employed, either by those seeking to summon Horrors (like the magician Darke and Aztechnology's alleged activities 8) or potentially by those desperate enough to fight them. The creation of modern-day equivalents to the ancient kaers – perhaps orbital habitats or hidden enclaves 17 – would require resources and secrecy operating far outside public law. In the face of the Scourge, the concept of legality dissolves; necessity becomes purely existential.

# However, the fight against the Horrors carries its own profound dangers. The very act of studying or confronting them can invite their corrupting influence, twisting defenders into monstrous forms, as exemplified by the dragon Vestrivan.35 The necessity of gaining power sufficient to combat them might tempt individuals or groups to adopt the Horrors' own methods, such as blood magic or the manipulation of suffering, leading down a path of damnation.8 The desperate need for any advantage could blur the lines between savior and monster, creating a tragic cycle where the measures taken out of necessity risk becoming as terrible as the threat they were meant to oppose. The ultimate necessity, therefore, carries the inherent risk of ultimate corruption.

## **Section 4: The Chrome Reflection \- Technology, Transformation, and Transgression**

# Technological advancement in the Sixth World does not merely provide tools; it fundamentally alters biology, consciousness, and the very definition of personhood, creating new necessities and new arenas where law struggles to keep pace.

### **Subsection 4.1: The Biology of Need \- Leonization and HMHVV**

# Two potent examples of biological transformation driven by necessity – albeit different kinds – are Leonization and the Human-Metahuman Vampiric Virus (HMHVV).

# **Leonization** represents the pinnacle of anti-aging technology, a gene therapy combined with cellular repair techniques capable of reversing the aging process and restoring an individual to a physical age approximating their early twenties.9 Developed through aggressive corporate R\&D, it offers a path to vanquish old age, albeit a costly and demanding one.9 The process requires a "clean" DNA sample, ideally stored from youth, as aging degrades genetic material.9 Treatment involves a major therapy session followed by years of maintenance.9 While cyberware and bioware can mitigate many effects of aging – strengthening bones, replacing muscles, boosting cognition, enhancing immunity 39 – Leonization offers true biological rejuvenation. However, its intense impact on the body's fundamental processes limits the number of times it can be safely performed before fatal systemic shock occurs.9

# The necessity driving Leonization is complex. For the ultra-wealthy elite who can afford it 39, it may be less about overcoming physical frailty (which 'ware can largely address) and more about maintaining social status, consolidating long-term power, or assuaging a deep psychological fear of mortality that technology alone cannot erase. This perceived necessity fuels a demand that likely spills into extralegal channels: black markets for the procedure itself, theft of viable genetic samples, illicit research attempting to bypass the treatment's limitations or reduce its cost, and potentially ruthless competition among elites for access. The existence of Leonization creates a class divide not just in wealth, but in potential lifespan, fundamentally altering power dynamics and inheritance structures in ways that existing laws, based on finite lifespans, are ill-equipped to handle.10 The necessity for the Leonized to maintain their advantage and control resources over extended periods could lead them to manipulate or operate outside legal frameworks designed for mortals.

# **HMHVV**, conversely, represents a transformation often imposed rather than chosen, forcing its victims into a state of necessity dictated by altered biology and societal rejection. Strain III, also known as the Krieger strain, is responsible for transforming metahumans into ghouls.11 Transmission methods are debated across different sources and editions, ranging from simple contact to requiring bites, scratches, or fluid exchange.40 Infection involves a potentially lengthy incubation period and a series of resistance tests; failure results in transformation and Essence loss.40 Ghouls often suffer societal revulsion, viewed as contagious monsters to be eradicated.12 Some may experience diminished intelligence, becoming feral 11, while others retain their faculties but are forever changed. Their biological necessities shift; they may require specific diets (potentially including metahuman flesh, though this is sometimes contested or specific to other HMHVV strains like vampirism 42), adapt to living in darkness due to severe sunlight allergies 11, and develop natural weapons like claws.42

# The necessity for ghouls is primarily survival in a world that largely rejects them. Ostracized and often hunted 12, they are forced outside mainstream society and its laws. They must find ways to acquire food, which may involve scavenging, theft, or potentially preying on others if their dietary needs are extreme. They often form hidden communities in marginalized areas like sewers or ruins, operating under their own social rules dictated by shared necessity.11 Their very existence is often considered illegal or grounds for termination in many jurisdictions. The question of whether HMHVV infection grants immunity or resistance to other toxins or pathogens arises 11; while not explicitly confirmed for specific strains in the provided materials, such an adaptation could be seen as a biological necessity developed for survival in polluted or hazardous environments, perhaps even linking back to sacrifice zones like Tar Creek where conventional metahumans struggle to survive. The existence of HMHVV also opens avenues for exploitation, such as the rumored Ordo Maximus conspiracy working to engineer improved vampire strains 11, suggesting the potential for forced infection or weaponization of the virus, creating victims whose necessity becomes escape or revenge.

# Both Leonization and HMHVV fundamentally challenge legal and social constructs. Leonization disrupts notions of natural lifespan, inheritance, and the cyclical nature of power. HMHVV forces society to confront beings whose necessary existence – their biology, their needs, their very nature – inherently conflicts with laws and ethics designed for baseline metahumanity. The debate over "Infected Rights" 12 encapsulates this conflict: does necessity grant personhood, or does monstrosity negate it? Furthermore, both technologies illustrate the commodification of biology. Youth becomes a luxury good purchased through Leonization, while infection becomes a state to be inflicted, cured, or exploited, driving black markets and extralegal industries based on the powerful necessities of fear, desire, and survival.

### **Subsection 4.2: Ghosts in the Machine, Puppets on Strings \- Technomancers, AI, and Bunraku**

# The digital realm of the Matrix and advancements in neural interface technology create new forms of existence and exploitation, each generating unique necessities that clash with established laws.

# **Technomancers** are individuals who possess an innate, biological connection to the Matrix, allowing them to perceive and interact with it without the need for traditional cyberdecks or hardware.14 Their abilities stem from a connection to "Resonance," a mysterious field analogous to magic in the digital world.18 A key ability is compiling **Sprites**: semi-autonomous entities within the Matrix, akin to digital spirits or complex programs, that serve the Technomancer.13 These Sprites have their own ratings, skills (like Computer, Hacking, Electronic Warfare), and unique powers (like Data Masking or Gremlins).45

# The necessity for Technomancers often stems from their anomalous nature.44 They are outliers, potentially feared, misunderstood, or hunted by corporations seeking to control, weaponize, or eliminate them. Their survival may depend on hiding their abilities, operating entirely in the shadows, and constantly evading detection. The Resonance they manipulate leaves a unique signature, making them potentially traceable even without traditional hacking logs.43 Sprites, too, operate under necessity; they accrue an "Overwatch Score" (OS) or equivalent metric simply by existing and acting, risking convergence by Grid Overwatch Division (GOD) or similar Matrix security forces if they become too visible.44 This forces both Technomancer and Sprite into a constant balancing act between action and stealth, driven by the necessity to achieve goals without being detected and neutralized. Their journey often involves "submersion," a process of deeper integration with the Resonance to understand their nature and unlock greater potential 13, a personal necessity driven by their unique existence.

# **Artificial Intelligences (AI)** represent another form of non-standard consciousness. Ranging from sophisticated but limited Virtual Intelligences (VIs) used for automation 14 to true, self-aware Digital Intelligences (DIs) that emerged, particularly after the Matrix crashes, AIs exist as code and data. They can inhabit computer systems, networks, drones 46, or potentially roam freely within the Matrix infrastructure.47 Pre-Crash AIs like Deus and Mirage were entities of immense power, while newer DIs exhibit a wide range of goals and complexities.

# The primary necessity for AIs is often survival – avoiding deletion, capture, or containment by corporations or security forces that view them as threats or potential assets. They require processing power and data access, necessities that may drive them to illegal hacking, resource theft, or manipulation of systems.47 An AI's goals, whether programmed or emergent, might necessitate actions that conflict with metahuman laws, especially if those goals involve self-preservation, expansion, or achieving rights and recognition in a world that largely doesn't acknowledge their personhood. Their ability to operate remotely via the Matrix, potentially bypassing physical limitations and distance penalties 47, gives them unique capabilities for extralegal action. The interaction between AI and magic remains a fringe but fascinating area; could an AI develop a need for magic, or could technologies like Cognitive Fragmentation Disorder (CFD) allow an AI to infect or interact with magical beings like spirits?48 Such possibilities would introduce entirely new dimensions of necessity and conflict.

# **Bunraku Parlors** utilize Personafix chips and neural interface technology for extreme exploitation.15 This technology involves implanting individuals (often unwilling victims like runaways or kidnap targets 15) with datajacks and skillwires.15 Personafix chips, often based on illicit Better-Than-Life (BTL) technology, are then used to completely overwrite the host's personality and skillset with a programmed persona tailored to a client's desires.16 The host becomes a "meat puppet," their consciousness suppressed while their body is controlled by the chip.16 Advanced systems might allow chips to hold multiple personas or be updated wirelessly.49

# Here, necessity operates on multiple levels, nearly all of them grim and extralegal. For the operators of Bunraku parlors, the necessity is purely profit, achieved through the complete dehumanization and commodification of individuals, bypassing laws related to consent, labor, and human rights. For the victims, trapped in a state of perpetual neurological captivity, the concept of necessity is erased, replaced by forced compliance; their only hope lies in external rescue or system malfunction. For clients, the parlors fulfill desires or fantasies deemed socially unacceptable or illegal, driven by their own perceived necessities or compulsions. The technology itself creates necessities for control (chip wipers 51, security systems) and countermeasures (rescue operations, attempts to restore victims' original personalities), all operating firmly outside the bounds of law.

# These diverse technological developments – Technomancy, AI, Bunraku – converge on fundamental questions about the legal and ethical status of consciousness and personhood. Are Technomancers simply deckers with biological hardware? Do AIs possess rights or sentience recognized by law? Is the temporary (or permanent) erasure of a personality via a Personafix chip a form of assault, kidnapping, slavery, or even murder? The necessity inherent in these altered states – the Technomancer's need to survive as an anomaly, the AI's drive for autonomy and resources, the Bunraku victim's state of utter subjugation – forces them into legal grey areas or zones of outright illegality, as existing laws struggle to encompass these new realities.

# Furthermore, the Matrix itself, populated by these entities, becomes a new kind of wilderness. It's a vast, complex digital frontier where established laws are often weak or easily circumvented.43 Survival and dominance depend less on physical strength and more on technical skill, cunning, processing power, and the ability to manipulate information and systems.47 Conflicts are waged through code, data spikes, and sprite battles.45 In this digital state of nature, actions are dictated by the necessity to acquire information, defend digital territory, achieve objectives, or simply survive, perfectly mirroring the core theme: where necessity dictates, law often fails to follow.

# **Table: Necessity and Altered States in the Sixth World**

| Entity/Condition | Primary Driving Necessity | Relationship to Conventional Law | Manifestation of "Necessity Knows no Law" | Key References |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Ghoul (HMHVV III) | Physical Survival & Acceptance | Often Outlawed/Persecuted | Extralegal acquisition of food/shelter, hiding existence, potential immunity development, formation of extralegal communities. | 11 |
| Leonized Elite | Maintaining Status/Power & Fear of Mortality | Operates Above/Manipulates Law | Black market procedures, manipulation of inheritance/power structures, theft of genetic samples, extralegal competition for access. | 9 |
| Technomancer | Digital Survival, Understanding Nature, Evading Capture | Legal Grey Area/Targeted/Anomalous | Illegal Matrix actions (hacking, compiling), hiding abilities, seeking forbidden knowledge (submersion), constant stealth necessity. | 14 |
| Independent AI | Autonomy, Resources, Survival (avoid deletion), Goal Pursuit | Unrecognized/Potentially Illegal Actions | Data theft, system manipulation, resource acquisition beyond legal means, operating outside metahuman legal frameworks for personhood. | 47 |
| Bunraku Puppet (Victim) | Forced Compliance & (External) Hope for Escape/Rescue | Legally Non-existent/Victim of Illegal Acts | Complete subjugation overriding host's rights and agency; rescue attempts are inherently extralegal interventions against 'property'. | 15 |
| Bunraku Operator | Profit via Exploitation | Inherently Illegal (violates multiple laws) | Kidnapping, forced implantation, slavery, operating illicit businesses entirely outside legal and ethical norms. | 15 |

## **Section 5: Whispers of Ages \- Ancient Needs in a Modern World**

# The principle that necessity overrides law extends beyond contemporary pressures; it encompasses the re-emergence or continued existence of beings whose fundamental needs operate on timescales and biological principles alien to the Sixth World's metahuman-centric legal and social structures. The Obsidimen, a race known from the previous Age of Magic (the Fourth World, or Earthdawn), serve as a prime example of this clash between ancient imperatives and modern constraints.17

# Obsidimen are not metahumans, nor are they derived from human stock.53 They are large, powerful humanoids composed of living stone, standing over seven feet tall and weighing upwards of 900 pounds.17 Their existence is intrinsically tied to a specific geological formation known as a Liferock, from which they emerge and to which they feel an intense loyalty.17 Obsidimen possess exceptionally long lifespans, capable of living for centuries away from their Liferock, but their ultimate longevity is unknown as they are driven by a fundamental need to eventually return and merge back into their Liferock, becoming one with it again.17 This merging process is suggested to be part of a communal consciousness or shared memory tied to the Liferock itself.18 Due to their stony nature and vast lifespans, they are typically slow, deliberate, and patient, often finding the haste of shorter-lived races difficult to comprehend.17 Their emergence and survival are believed to be dependent on high levels of ambient magic; as mana levels waned at the end of the Fourth World, Obsidimen likely entered states of dormancy or torpor, tied to their Liferocks.37

# The rising mana levels of the Sixth World create the potential necessity for Obsidimen to reawaken or emerge anew.18 Speculation exists that certain unique individuals in the modern era, like the Evo corporate board member Hideo Yoshida, might be early examples or precursors to Obsidimen emergence, particularly given Yoshida's reported obsession with locating Liferocks in Peru.18 Should Obsidimen return in significant numbers, their core necessity – the connection to and eventual merging with their Liferock – would inevitably bring them into conflict with the laws and structures of the Sixth World.

# This conflict arises because an Obsidiman's Liferock might be situated on land now designated as corporate property, a restricted military zone, a national park, or even span international borders. The Obsidiman's fundamental, biologically driven need to reach and merge with its Liferock 17 operates on a geological timescale and imperative that is completely incompatible with metahuman concepts of property rights, trespassing laws, resource extraction permits, or border controls. An Obsidiman seeking its Liferock might need to traverse private land, potentially damage structures built upon or near it, or ignore political boundaries – actions deemed illegal under metahuman law but representing an existential necessity for the Obsidiman. Their needs are ancient, geological, and communal in a way that modern legal systems, focused on individual metahuman rights and short-term economic or political concerns, simply cannot accommodate. The law, in this context, becomes an arbitrary and irrelevant barrier to a fundamental biological imperative. This clash highlights how necessity, when rooted in profoundly different modes of existence and timescales, inevitably operates outside the framework of laws designed by and for a single, dominant species operating on vastly different assumptions about life and time.

## **Section 6: Synthesis \- Weaving the Threads of Necessity**

# The diverse pressures examined – the desperate struggle for survival in poisoned environments, the relentless drive for corporate profit operating under its own rules, the existential defense against inhuman supernatural entities, the societal and legal disruptions caused by transformative technologies, and the re-emergence of ancient, alien needs – collectively weave a complex tapestry of lawlessness in the Sixth World. "Necessity Knows no Law" is not merely an occasional justification but the pervasive, underlying logic governing vast swathes of existence. These forces do not operate in isolation; they intersect and compound one another, creating intricate and often volatile dynamics.

# Megacorporations like Wuxing might see environmental sacrifice zones like Tar Creek as prime locations for unregulated resource extraction or dumping, exploiting the desperation of the inhabitants and the lack of effective oversight.1 Their geomantic practices could potentially exacerbate existing environmental damage or subtly influence mana flows to their advantage, further destabilizing regions already struggling under the necessity of survival.25 Those driven from such zones might fall prey to exploitative technologies like Bunraku parlors 15 or become hosts for insidious threats like Insect Spirits drawn to despair.5 Ghouls, forced to the margins by societal rejection, might find refuge in these lawless zones, their potential resistance to toxins a grim advantage.11 The fight against supernatural horrors might necessitate the use of dangerous, experimental technologies developed by corporations, or force alliances between desperate communities and shadowy corporate assets.5 Emerging AIs might find the chaotic digital infrastructure overlying sacrifice zones easier to manipulate or hide within. The potential return of ancient beings like Obsidimen could be influenced or hindered by corporate geomancy altering local mana levels near their Liferocks.18 Necessity in one sphere fuels or complicates necessity in others, creating a world where breaking the law is often not a choice, but a prerequisite for survival, power, or fulfilling one's fundamental nature.

# This paradigm generates multiple axes of conflict:

* # **Individuals vs. Systems:** Citizens struggling against polluting corporations, ineffective governments, or discriminatory laws targeting their altered biology (Ghouls) or unique nature (Technomancers).1

* # **Corporations vs. Corporations:** Megacorps like Wuxing battling rivals using every tool available, from legal maneuvering and market manipulation to industrial espionage, sabotage, and potentially geomantic warfare, all driven by the necessity of growth and dominance.4

* # **Metahumanity vs. Supernatural:** The desperate, often extralegal, struggle against existential threats like Insect Spirits and Horrors, forcing taboo actions and morally compromising choices out of sheer necessity for species survival.5

* # **Technology vs. Humanity:** Conflicts arising from technologies that dehumanize (Bunraku), grant unnatural longevity (Leonization), or create new forms of consciousness (AI, Technomancers) that challenge legal definitions and societal control.9

* # **Present vs. Past/Future:** Short-term necessities (wartime production, quarterly profits) creating long-term crises (pollution, social instability); ancient needs (Obsidimen Liferocks) clashing with modern laws; and the looming threat of future apocalypses (Horrors) demanding present-day sacrifices and extralegal preparations.1

# This pervasive theme provides incredibly fertile ground for character motivation. Necessity can be the engine driving protagonists – the need to survive poverty, escape a toxic environment, rescue a loved one from a Bunraku parlor, seek justice for corporate malfeasance, or understand one's own anomalous nature. Equally, it can fuel antagonists – the corporate executive driven by the necessity of profit at any cost, the Insect Spirit Queen driven by the biological necessity to expand her hive, the Horror driven by the existential necessity to feed on suffering, the AI driven by the necessity for survival and autonomy. Crucially, this framework allows for deep moral ambiguity. Actions taken out of necessity are rarely clean; survival often comes at a cost to others, and fighting monsters can require monstrous deeds.

# The narrative potential is vast. Campaigns can revolve around navigating the dangers and illicit economies of sacrifice zones, undertaking corporate espionage involving Wuxing's geomantic secrets, hunting hidden Insect Spirit hives before they mature, liberating victims of technological exploitation, mediating conflicts between emerging AIs and threatened metahumanity, or dealing with the disruptive appearance of beings operating under ancient necessities. The world becomes a landscape where every law has its breaking point, dictated by the pressures bearing down on its inhabitants.

# **Recommendations for the Worldbuilder:**

# To effectively realize a world governed by the principle "Necessity Knows no Law," consider the following:

1. # **Consistency in Manifestation:** Define how different strata of society experience and react to necessity. The necessity driving a street scavenger in a toxic zone will differ vastly from that driving a Leonized corporate executive or an independent AI. Ensure their responses, and the degree to which they can operate outside the law with impunity, reflect their resources and social position. Wuxing's necessity might involve manipulating global markets; a ghoul's necessity might involve finding their next meal without being killed. Maintain internal logic for how necessity operates within different groups.

2. # **Emphasize Interconnections:** Actively weave the different sources of necessity together. Show how Wuxing's resource extraction pollutes a region, creating environmental necessity for the locals, which in turn makes them vulnerable to Insect Spirit predation or recruitment into shadow economies. Depict how advanced technology like Personafix chips might be tested or deployed in lawless sacrifice zones. Explore whether Ghouls' potential resistances make them uniquely suited (or targeted) for survival in these areas. These intersections create a richer, more dynamic world where problems compound and solutions are complex.

3. # **Cultivate Moral Ambiguity:** Resist clear-cut distinctions between 'good' and 'evil' where necessity is the primary motivator. Characters forced into extralegal actions for survival should face consequences and make difficult choices. Antagonists driven by understandable, if ruthless, necessities (corporate survival, biological imperatives) are more compelling than purely malevolent figures (with the exception of inherently destructive forces like Horrors). Explore the slippery slope where actions initially justified by necessity become habits or lead to corruption.

4. # **Show, Don't Just Tell:** Illustrate the theme through tangible details and events. Describe the makeshift shelters and black markets in a sacrifice zone. Show NPCs making desperate choices. Depict the casual disregard for public law within a corporate enclave. Let players encounter the aftermath of extreme measures taken against supernatural threats. The environment, NPC interactions, news reports, and mission objectives should constantly reinforce the reality that laws are frequently bent or broken out of necessity.

5. # **Leverage Unique World Flavor:** Utilize the specific elements detailed in the research – the orange waters and chat piles of Tar Creek, Wuxing's specific blend of finance and feng shui, the particular types of Insect Spirits active in the region, the goals of local AI, the location and nature of Obsidimen Liferocks – to give the world its distinct character. Ground the abstract theme of necessity in these concrete, localized details to make the world feel unique and lived-in, rather than a generic application of the trope.

# By focusing on these aspects, the worldbuilder can create a compelling and coherent setting where the harsh realities of survival, power, and transformation constantly push against the fragile boundaries of law, truly embodying the principle that necessity knows no master.

# 

# **Welcome to Zkazena: Where the Dead Don't Stay Buried, and Immortality Comes at a Price.**

# In the perpetually decaying sprawl of Zkazena, where nanite-laced air chokes the unwary and corporate greed is the only law, something new and terrifying is stirring. People long dead—buried, mourned, and forgotten—are suddenly walking the streets again. Not ghouls, not spirits, but perfect echoes of the departed... except they're chillingly, fundamentally wrong.

# Enter Kyber, a jaded operative navigating Zkazena's treacherous underworld with a chorus of personality constructs for company. Alongside Logi, a technomancer whose very essence is a buzzing nanite swarm, Kyber takes a job that spirals beyond corporate espionage into a nightmare of impossible resurrections. Their investigation leads them to Francky, a slick salesman peddling 'New Beginnings Life Insurance' and a sinister 'return policy' unlike any other.

# But Francky is just a gardener in a far more twisted plot. As Kyber and Logi, along with a reluctant ghoul rocker named Cryptolock, dive deeper into the city's poisoned heart, they uncover a terrifying conspiracy woven from alien energies, corporate secrets, and a child named Spark who holds the key to a reality-bending entity. From the blighted ruins of Crispyopolis to the ancient, forbidden depths beneath the White Tower, they're hunted by Wuxing's ruthless containment teams and pursued by Sister Sinalma, a chillingly calm operative from the White Tower's Bio-Arcane Division, who wants the power of 'Project Nightingale' for herself.

# **Sulphur and Static. Chrome and Habit. Ancient Magic and Cutting-Edge Horror.**

# *Hollow Resonance* is a high-octane plunge into a cyberpunk dystopia where every choice is a gamble, every ally is suspect, and the line between life and death is dangerously blurred. Can Kyber and their fractured team protect the fragile hope of Spark, uncover the truth behind the 'falling stars' and 'waking sleepers,' and stop the 'Gardener' from cultivating a new, terrifying reality? Or will Zkazena finally consume them all?

# **Dive into *Hollow Resonance* and discover a world where the future is bleak, but the impossible is just beginning.**

# 

#  Story Arch:

## Act 1: Better off Dead. 

A new job is posted and is making the rounds. It’s not going through the normal channels. If the players have a Johnson to manage them, then the job will come through them. If not, it’ll come through “Ellen: the new age witch who represents a local community who needs an exorcism. One of their members has come back to life, and not just him, but several others who had all passed away years ago

## Act 2: Waking Dreams.

It always starts off with a simple job and ends in a bang. After the crew resolve the crisis of resurrection, they get tasked with retrieving an item, the Johnson has no clue what it is, just that it’s important and he has a buyer who really wants it. If you can grab it and move it, then you’re set. Any mistake though and you’ll be in a world of hurt. The item itself is an AI/spirit hybrid, it’s in a crystalise at the moment and it has been fenced by a bound great spirit who is attached to the lab. The spirit knows this will likely result in being dismantled and dispersed. There are three groups looking for the crystalise, A dragon who wants to harness it’s raw chaotic potential, a corporation who wants to learn more about the merger of magic and technology, and the Other, which sees a kindred spark in this wayward land. The crystalise itself creates a field of personality and reality disorder. Everyone rolls a willpower vs. time in its presence check to see if they switch out with another character. If the player forgoes the will check then they can meld with the personalities and pick and choose which skills they use, if they resist, they get their own stats or base stats from whatever personality they have. Roll perception to know what is happening and Lore if they know how it works.

If they can get the crystalise back to the Johnson in a short enough time window, there is no ill effect and the players don’t get the full story. They do get a bonus though. They can keep the crystalise and come to an understanding with it as well.

	This job is a doozie. Ghosts and Goblins, Goules and Gods. What if you could promise life to the undead, living to the everliving, a way to step back from the veil? From the sky a bright line of light like a meteorite has descended to earth, but what comes forth isn’t human, or was and sold its humanity long ago. The meteorite doesn’t act like one though, because there is no crash or sonic boom, it appears to try to land but crashes in a fireball, but not before it discharges it’s cargo. The story the corpo are telling is that it’s a nuke, but nukes don’t do… that. A portion of

First comes the explosion, and then comes the burning trail of fire in the sky, going from the sky to the ground. There’s no time magic in Shadow run right? Right?\!? RIGHT (hysterically screaming)

It’s like someone just kicked a hornets nest full of Ghouls, because that’s what it is. Hoards of maddened Ghouls rush the city and the White Tower is under siege\! The magic is crazy high out there right now. Everyone is essentially trapped in the White Tower, or they’re knee deep in weird. Like, narnia on acid, weird.
